subject: Re: Security deep-dive & hosting path — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Security deep-dive & hosting path — follow-up and next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so the team at Elara has what you need to evaluate hosting options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC/on-prem):

Summary from today's discovery:
- Use case: patient intake and triage routing; PHI may be processed for symptom extraction and triage suggestions.
- Primary requirement: HIPAA compliance + executed BAA.
- Constraints: regional data residency in US, audit evidence (SOC2 Type II) and detailed access logs required for internal audit.
- Performance: expected sustained ~60 reqs/min (peak bursts to ~250 reqs/min) with average request size ~450 tokens.

Action items we agreed on:
1) Attached: Redwood security questionnaire (filled) and a POC infra diagram. Please review and confirm any gaps.
2) You mentioned procurement & legal will need our SOC2 report, BAA language, and encryption details — I attached our SOC2 summary and a checklist.
3) Preliminary hosting recommendation (based on constraints): Dedicated capacity with Private VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. This gives predictable performance and aligns with BAA requirements. Hosted API is possible with an executed BAA but has different isolation characteristics — we'll enumerate the tradeoffs below.

Quick technical notes for procurement/legal:
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. We support customer KMS (AWS KMS/HSM integrations) for key separation.
- Audit logs: Token-level request logs and admin audit trails available; retention configurable (default 90 days, options to extend).
- Data retention & redaction: We offer request-level retention policies and a discard-on-ingest option for PHI in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- SOC2: Redwood holds SOC2 Type II; full report available under NDA.

Questions for you (so we can include precise answers in the questionnaire):
- Who is the primary legal contact for BAA negotiation and expected timeline for review?
- Any hard constraints on data residency beyond "US" (specific states or clouds)?
- Expected contract start date / desired go-live window for POC vs production?

Proposed next meeting: 45-minute security deep-dive (technical + legal attendees) — Wed Aug 13, 10:00–10:45 PT. Does that work?

I'll also loop in Karthik and Marissa internally to draft the dedicated/VPC configuration and a short SOW for the reserved capacity option.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Emma Chen <emma@elarahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elara Health Security <security@elarahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 18:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security deep-dive & hosting path — follow-up and next steps

Mina — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: we do process PHI in the flows you described and will need an executed BAA before any PHI is sent to Redwood systems. Our security team listed the following non-negotiables:

- SOC2 Type II (we will need the report under NDA)
- Customer KMS support (separate keys for prod)
- VPC peering between Elara and Redwood for Dedicated; if Hosted is proposed, strict tenant isolation and evidence of segmentation controls required
- Audit logging with immutable retention (minimum 1 year) and the ability to export logs to our SIEM
- Pen test and vulnerability scanning cadence evidence

On hosting preference: as we discussed on the call, Elara's SRE prefers Dedicated with VPC peering for production because of predictable performance and network-level isolation. We are open to a Hosted POC for speed to value if the BAA and isolation evidence are acceptable, but production should be Dedicated or Private (if you support on-prem).

Procurement & legal: legal@elarahealth.com will take lead on BAA and contract timeline. We aim to complete procurement and be in a POC by October 1.

I've attached a short Elara security requirements document for your review.

--Emma
Emma Chen
Product Security Lead, Elara Health
emma@elarahealth.com
Attachment: Elara_Security_Requirements.pdf

Team — quick internal summary and recommended response to Elara:

Key confirmations to provide (draft answers):
- SOC2: provide Type II report under NDA. We should attach the most recent report and an executive summary.
- KMS / encryption: we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted API supports bring-your-own-key via KMS in partner clouds (clarify per-cloud).
- VPC peering & network isolation: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private subnets; we can also offer AWS PrivateLink in certain regions.
- Audit logs: request-level telemetry and admin audit logs are available. Default retention 90 days; can extend to 365 days for an add-on. Exports to S3/SIEM are supported via a secure delivery pipeline.
- Pen tests: annual 3rd-party pen test and quarterly vuln scans; evidence available on request.

Recommended hosting path: propose a POC on Dedicated capacity with VPC peering using reserved small-medium pool (to match 60 reqs/min sustained, handle 250 reqs/min bursts). Include optional 1-month Hosted trial for early functional validation (no PHI until BAA is signed).

Next steps I propose we send to Emma (CC legal & procurement):
1) Send SOC2 executive summary + standard BAA draft (legal to review).
2) Share a concise Dedicated config + cost estimate and a short SOW for reserved capacity.
3) Schedule the security deep-dive (Mina to finalize with Elara).

I've uploaded a draft SOW and the Dedicated configuration worksheet to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB_example_doc
I'll also start scoping costs for 12-month vs 3-month reserved capacity and include autoscaling/burst options.

-Karthik
